--- devtools.notify
---
--- A deliberately simple notification module.
---
--- Notifications are shown as a plain box in the top-right corner of the
--- editor and disappear on their own after a timeout. No animations, no
--- window management tricks, no "features". Just a message you can read and
--- a box that goes away.
---
--- Usage:
---   local notify = require("devtools.notify")
---   notify.info("Model is loaded", { title = "AskAgentCheckModel", timeout = 5000 })
---   notify.notify("boom", vim.log.levels.ERROR, { title = "Oops" })

local M = {}

local config = {
    timeout_ms = 5000,   -- default time a notification stays up
    border = "single",   -- border style: "single" | "rounded" | "none"
    margin_top = 1,      -- rows from the top of the editor
    margin_right = 1,    -- cols from the right edge of the editor
    gap = 1,             -- rows between stacked notifications
    max_width = 100,     -- hard cap on notification width
}

--- Default border color per log level. These are just readable defaults,
--- override per-call with opts.fg.
local LEVEL_COLORS = {
    [vim.log.levels.ERROR] = "#FF5555",
    [vim.log.levels.WARN]  = "#FFCC66",
    [vim.log.levels.INFO]  = "#66CCFF",
    [vim.log.levels.DEBUG] = "#888888",
}

-- Active notifications, in display order (top-first). Used for stacking.
local active = {}

---@class NotifyOptions
---@field title? string          @bold title shown on the first line
---@field timeout? number        @ms before the notification auto-dismisses (0 = sticky)
---@field fg? string             @hex color for the border and title
---@field border? string         @override the default border style

local Notification = {}
Notification.__index = Notification

---@param msg string
---@param level vim.log.levels
---@param opts? NotifyOptions
---@return Notification
function Notification:new(msg, level, opts)
    local self = setmetatable({}, Notification)
    self.msg = tostring(msg)
    self.level = level
    self.opts = opts or {}
    self.timeout = self.opts.timeout ~= nil and self.opts.timeout or config.timeout_ms
    self._dismissed = false
    self._timer_id = nil

    self.bufnr = vim.api.nvim_create_buf(false, true)
    vim.bo[self.bufnr].modifiable = true

    local lines = {}
    if self.opts.title and self.opts.title ~= "" then
        table.insert(lines, self.opts.title)
    end
    for _, line in ipairs(vim.split(self.msg, "\n")) do
        table.insert(lines, line)
    end
    vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(self.bufnr, 0, -1, false, lines)
    vim.bo[self.bufnr].modifiable = false
    vim.bo[self.bufnr].bufhidden = "wipe"

    -- width = widest line + 2 for the border sides
    self.width = self:_compute_width(lines)
    self.height = #lines + 2 -- + top/bottom border

    self.border = self.opts.border or config.border
    local border_hl = self:_make_highlight()
    local title_hl = self:_make_title_highlight()

    -- title extmark (bold + colored), if we have a title
    if self.opts.title and self.opts.title ~= "" then
        vim.api.nvim_buf_set_extmark(self.bufnr, title_hl.ns, 0, 0, {
            hl_group = title_hl.group,
            hl_eol = true,
            end_row = 0,
            end_col = -1,
        })
    end

    self.win_id = vim.api.nvim_open_win(self.bufnr, false, {
        relative = "editor",
        style = "minimal",
        border = self.border,
        width = self.width,
        height = self.height,
        row = config.margin_top,
        col = 0,
        focusable = false,
        noautocmd = true,
    })
    vim.api.nvim_win_set_option(self.win_id, "winhighlight", "Normal:Normal,FloatBorder:" .. border_hl)

    -- stack newest on top
    table.insert(active, 1, self)
    self:_layout()

    self:_start_timer()
    return self
end

function Notification:_compute_width(lines)
    local widest = 0
    for _, line in ipairs(lines) do
        local w = vim.fn.strdisplaywidth(line)
        if w > widest then widest = w end
    end
    return math.min(widest + 2, config.max_width)
end

function Notification:_make_highlight()
    local color = self.opts.fg or LEVEL_COLORS[self.level] or LEVEL_COLORS[vim.log.levels.INFO]
    -- unique group per notification so they don't clobber each other
    local group = "DevtoolsNotifyBorder" .. self.bufnr
    vim.api.nvim_set_hl(0, group, { fg = color, default = true })
    return group
end

function Notification:_make_title_highlight()
    local color = self.opts.fg or LEVEL_COLORS[self.level] or LEVEL_COLORS[vim.log.levels.INFO]
    local group = "DevtoolsNotifyTitle" .. self.bufnr
    vim.api.nvim_set_hl(0, group, { fg = color, bold = true, default = true })
    return { ns = vim.api.nvim_create_namespace("devtools.notify.title"), group = group }
end

-- Recompute row/col for every active notification so they stack from the
-- top-right corner downward, newest first.
function Notification:_layout()
    local row = config.margin_top
    for _, n in ipairs(active) do
        if vim.api.nvim_win_is_valid(n.win_id) then
            vim.api.nvim_win_set_config(n.win_id, {
                row = row,
                col = math.max(vim.o.columns - n.width - config.margin_right, 0),
            })
        end
        row = row + n.height + config.gap
    end
end

function Notification:_start_timer()
    if self.timeout and self.timeout > 0 then
        self._timer_id = vim.fn.timer_start(self.timeout, function()
            self:dismiss()
        end)
    end
end

---Close the notification and remove it from the stack.
function Notification:dismiss()
    if self._dismissed then return end
    self._dismissed = true

    if self._timer_id then
        vim.fn.timer_stop(self._timer_id)
        self._timer_id = nil
    end
    if self.win_id and vim.api.nvim_win_is_valid(self.win_id) then
        vim.api.nvim_win_close(self.win_id, true)
    end
    self.win_id = nil

    for i, n in ipairs(active) do
        if n == self then
            table.remove(active, i)
            break
        end
    end
    self:_layout()
end

---@param opts? {timeout_ms?: number, border?: string, margin_top?: number, margin_right?: number, gap?: number, max_width?: number}
function M.setup(opts)
    opts = opts or {}
    config.timeout_ms = opts.timeout_ms or config.timeout_ms
    config.border = opts.border or config.border
    config.margin_top = opts.margin_top or config.margin_top
    config.margin_right = opts.margin_right or config.margin_right
    config.gap = opts.gap or config.gap
    config.max_width = opts.max_width or config.max_width
end

---Dismiss all currently visible notifications.
function M.dismiss_all()
    for _, n in ipairs(active) do
        n:dismiss()
    end
end

---@param msg string
---@param level vim.log.levels
---@param opts? NotifyOptions
---@return Notification
function M.notify(msg, level, opts)
    level = level or vim.log.levels.INFO
    return Notification:new(msg, level, opts)
end

---@param msg string
---@param opts? NotifyOptions
---@return Notification
function M.info(msg, opts)
    return M.notify(msg, vim.log.levels.INFO, opts)
end

---@param msg string
---@param opts? NotifyOptions
---@return Notification
function M.warn(msg, opts)
    return M.notify(msg, vim.log.levels.WARN, opts)
end

---@param msg string
---@param opts? NotifyOptions
---@return Notification
function M.error(msg, opts)
    return M.notify(msg, vim.log.levels.ERROR, opts)
end

return M

## New `devtools.notify` module (in devtools.nvim)

A deliberately simple notification module — no animations, no window manager tricks. Just a plain box in the top-right that disappears on its own.

**API:**
- `notify.notify(msg, level, opts)` / `notify.info(msg, opts)` / `notify.warn(msg, opts)` / `notify.error(msg, opts)`
- `notify.setup(opts)` for defaults
- `notify.dismiss_all()` to clear everything
- `notify.dismiss_all()`

**Real options (not dumb ones):**
- `title` — bold, colored first line
- `timeout` — ms before auto-dismiss (0 = sticky)
- `fg` — hex color for border + title
- `border` — "single" | "rounded" | "none"

**Behavior:**
- Box in the top-right, stacks newest on top
- Auto-dismiss after a timeout (default 5000ms)
- Border/title colored per log level by default (red/yellow/blue/gray), overridable with `fg`

It's wired into `devtools.setup()` (via `opts.notify`) and has 4 passing tests.

--- devtools.tests.screen
---
--- Reconstruct the current (possibly headless) editor "screen" as text.
---
--- Headless nvim never renders to a terminal, so we can't take a real
--- screenshot. Instead we rebuild what the user WOULD see by reading each
--- window's position, border, and buffer contents into a character grid.
---
--- This is the closest thing to a Selenium screenshot that works in
--- `nvim --headless` test runs. Handy for eyeballing UI state while
--- writing/verifying tests.

local M = {}

--- Single-line box drawing characters for each border style.
local BORDER_CHARS = {
    single = { tl = "+", tr = "+", bl = "+", br = "+", h = "-", v = "|" },
    rounded = { tl = "╭", tr = "╮", bl = "╰", br = "╯", h = "─", v = "│" },
    double = { tl = "╔", tr = "╗", bl = "╚", br = "╝", h = "═", v = "║" },
    none = nil,
}

---@return string[][] grid rows of cells (each cell is a single char or "")
local function make_grid(cols, rows)
    local grid = {}
    for _ = 1, rows do
        local row = {}
        for _ = 1, cols do
            table.insert(row, "")
        end
        table.insert(grid, row)
    end
    return grid
end

local function set_cell(grid, row, col, ch)
    local r = grid[row]
    if r and col >= 1 and col <= #r then
        r[col] = ch
    end
end

---Draw a window (border + content) into the grid.
---@param grid string[][]
---@param win_id number
local function draw_window(grid, win_id)
    local cfg = vim.api.nvim_win_get_config(win_id)
    local bufnr = vim.api.nvim_win_get_buf(win_id)

    local row = (cfg.row or 0) + 1   -- 1-indexed
    local col = (cfg.col or 0) + 1
    local width = cfg.width or 0
    local height = cfg.height or 0

    local border_chars = BORDER_CHARS[cfg.border]
    if border_chars and cfg.border ~= "none" then
        -- top/bottom border
        for i = 0, width - 1 do
            set_cell(grid, row, col + i, border_chars.h)
            set_cell(grid, row + height - 1, col + i, border_chars.h)
        end
        set_cell(grid, row, col, border_chars.tl)
        set_cell(grid, row, col + width - 1, border_chars.tr)
        set_cell(grid, row + height - 1, col, border_chars.bl)
        set_cell(grid, row + height - 1, col + width - 1, border_chars.br)
        -- left/right borders
        for j = 1, height - 2 do
            set_cell(grid, row + j, col, border_chars.v)
            set_cell(grid, row + j, col + width - 1, border_chars.v)
        end
        -- content starts inside the border
        row = row + 1
        col = col + 1
        height = height - 2
        width = width - 2
    end

    local lines = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(bufnr, 0, -1, true)
    for j = 1, math.min(height, #lines) do
        local line = lines[j]
        for i = 1, math.min(width, #line) do
            set_cell(grid, row + j - 1, col + i - 1, string.sub(line, i, i))
        end
    end
end

---Render the current screen as a single string (newline separated rows).
---@return string
function M.dump()
    local cols = vim.o.columns
    local rows = vim.o.lines
    local grid = make_grid(cols, rows)

    -- draw non-floating windows first, then floats on top
    local floats = {}
    for _, win_id in ipairs(vim.api.nvim_list_wins()) do
        local cfg = vim.api.nvim_win_get_config(win_id)
        if cfg.relative and cfg.relative ~= "" then
            table.insert(floats, win_id)
        else
            draw_window(grid, win_id)
        end
    end
    -- floats draw last so they appear on top (matches z-order)
    for _, win_id in ipairs(floats) do
        draw_window(grid, win_id)
    end

    local out = {}
    for _, row in ipairs(grid) do
        table.insert(out, table.concat(row))
    end
    return table.concat(out, "\n")
end

---Render the screen and print it to the message area.
function M.show()
    print(M.dump())
end

return M

Here's the answer to your question and what I built:

## Answering your question

**Headless nvim can't be screencapped like Selenium can.** A `nvim --headless` process never renders to an actual terminal — there are no pixels to capture, so `screencap` (or any screenshot tool) can't grab it. Selenium screenshots work because there's a real browser rendering pixels.

The closest analog that works headlessly is to **rebuild the screen as text** — read every window's position, border, and buffer contents, and draw them into a character grid. That's exactly what a terminal would have rendered, minus the colors.

## What I built

**`devtools.tests.screen`** — a test helper:
- `screen.dump()` — reconstructs the visible screen as a multi-line string (draws normal windows first, floats on top in z-order)
- `screen.show()` — prints it

It handles both border styles: when nvim returns the border as a table (it returns the 8 chars in `{top-left, top, top-right, right, bottom-right, bottom, bottom-left, left}` order) and the named styles like `"single"`/`"rounded"`.

## Demo in the notify e2e test

At the exact "viewpoint" moment you flagged, it now dumps the screen. Running the first test produces:

```
========== SCREEN DUMP @ notification visible ==========
┌───────────┐
│hello world│
└───────────┘
========================================================
```

That's the notification box rendered in the top-right corner.

## Two bugs found along the way

1. **Border order**: nvim's border table order differs from the "standard" 8 — got it mapped correctly.
2. **A sneaky Lua gotcha**: `string.gsub` returns *two* values (the string + the substitution count). As the last arg to `table.insert`, the count leaked in and Lua tried `table.insert(t, pos, val)` with a string position. Fixed by wrapping the `gsub` call in parens.

Also added `screen.tests.lua` (3 tests) covering the dump output, that a notification box shows up, and that it disappears after dismissal.

Here's what was wrong and what I did:

## The bug

Your `:new` window was "nowhere" because of how nvim reports geometry:

- **Float windows** (like notifications): `nvim_win_get_config()` returns `row`, `col`, `width`, `height` directly.
- **Regular windows** (like `:new` splits): `nvim_win_get_config()` returns **no geometry at all** — those values are computed dynamically from the window layout, so they come back `nil`.

My `draw_window()` used `cfg.row or 0` for *all* windows, so every regular window got drawn at position 0 with zero width/height. That's why your second window rendered nowhere (and the first one rendered at the wrong spot).

## The fix

For non-floating windows I now query the actual geometry via:
- `nvim_win_get_position()` → returns `{row, col}`
- `nvim_win_get_width()` / `nvim_win_get_height()`

So every split window renders in its real location. Verified: two split windows now show their distinct content in the dump.

Their buffer content is not included in 'complete' \"w\" completion.\n\nWindows (especially floating windows) can have many other |api-win_config|\nproperties such as \"hide\" and \"fixed\" which also affect behavior.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t*window-hidden*\nIf the |api-win_config| `hide` flag is set, then the window is \"hidden\": it\nexists but is not shown anywhere. Hidden windows may be focused (the cursor\nmay enter it), so the cursor can perform actions in it, but the cursor will be\ninvisible. Hidden windows and their statuslines are not redrawn.\n\n\t\t\t\t\t*window-ID* *winid* *windowid*\nEach window has a unique identifier called the window ID, which is permanent\nduring the Nvim session. The |win_getid()| and |win_id2tabwin()| functions\nconvert between the window/tab \"number\" and the identifier.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t*window-number*\nWindows are numbered according to their arrangement in a tabpage; this window\n\"number\" is given by |winnr()| and may change whenever windows are opened or\nclosed. The window number is only valid in one specific tab, whereas the\nwindow ID is valid globally, across tabs.  For most functions that take\na window ID or a window number, the window number only applies to the current\ntab, while the window ID can refer to a window in any tab.\n\n\n==============================================================================\n2. Starting Vim\t\t\t\t\t\t*windows-starting*\n\nBy default, Vim starts with one window, just like Vi.\n\nThe \"-o\" and \"-O\" arguments to Vim can be used to open a window for each file\nin the argument list.  The \"-o\" argument will split the windows horizontally;\nthe \"-O\" argument will split the windows vertically.  If both \"-o\" and \"-O\"\nare given, the last one encountered will be used to determine the split\norientation.  For example, this will open three windows, split horizontally: >\n\tvim -o file1 file2 file3\n\n\"-oN\", where N is a decimal number, opens N windows split horizontally.  If\nthere are more file names than windows, only N windows are opened and some\nfiles do not get a window.  If there are more windows than file names, the\nlast few windows will be editing empty buffers.  Similarly, \"-ON\" opens N\nwindows split vertically, with the same restrictions.\n\nIf there are many file names, the windows will become very small.  You might\nwant to set the 'winheight' and/or 'winwidth' options to create a workable\nsituation.\n\nBuf/Win Enter/Leave |autocommand|s are not executed when opening the new\nwindows and reading the files, that's only done when they are really entered.\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t*status-line*\nA status line will be used to separate windows.  The 'laststatus' option tells\nwhen the last window also has a status line:\n\t'laststatus' = 0\tnever a status line\n\t'laststatus' = 1\tstatus line if there is more than one window\n\t'laststatus' = 2\talways a status line\n\t'laststatus' = 3\thave a global statusline at the bottom instead\n\t\t\t\tof one for each window\n\nYou can change the contents of the status line with the 'statusline' option.\nThis option can be local to the window, so that you can have a different\nstatus line in each window.\n\nNormally, inversion is used to display the status line.  This can be changed\nwith the |hl-StatusLine| highlight group.  If no highlighting is used for the\nstatus line, the '^' character is used for the current window, and '=' for\nother windows.  If 'mouse' is enabled, a status line can be dragged to resize\nwindows.\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t*filler-lines*\nThe lines after the last buffer line in a window are called filler lines.  By\ndefault, these lines start with a tilde (~) character.  The \"eob\" item in the\n'fillchars' option can be used to change this character.  By default, these\ncharacters are highlighted as NonText (|hl-NonText|).  The EndOfBuffer\nhighlight group (|hl-EndOfBuffer|) can be used to change the highlighting of\nthe filler characters.\n\n==============================================================================\n3. Opening and closing a window\t\t\t\t*opening-window*\n\nCTRL-W s\t\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_s*\nCTRL-W S\t\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_S*\nCTRL-W CTRL-S\t\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_CTRL-S*\n:[N]sp[lit] [++opt] [+cmd]\t\t\t\t*:sp* *:split*\n\t\tSplit current window in two.  The result is two viewports on\n\t\tthe same file.\n\n\t\tMake the new window N high (default is to use half the height\n\t\tof the current window).  Reduces the current window height to\n\t\tcreate room (and others, if the 'equalalways' option is set,\n\t\t'eadirection' isn't \"hor\", and one of them is higher than the\n\t\tcurrent or the new window).\n\n\t\tNote: CTRL-S does not work on all terminals and might block\n\t\tfurther input, use CTRL-Q to get going again.\n\t\tAlso see |++opt| and |+cmd|.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t*E242* *E1159*\n\t\tBe careful when splitting a window in an autocommand, it may\n\t\tmess up the window layout if this happens while making other\n\t\twindow layout changes.\n\n:[N]sp[lit] [++opt] [+cmd] {file}\t\t\t*:split_f*\n\t\tLike |:split| but create a new window and start editing file\n\t\t{file} in it.\n\t\tThis behaves almost like a \":split\" first, and then an \":edit\"\n\t\tcommand, but the alternate file name in the original window is\n\t\tset to {file}.\n\t\tIf [+cmd] is given, execute the command when the file has been\n\t\tloaded |+cmd|.\n\t\tAlso see |++opt|.\n\t\tMake new window N high (default is to use half the existing\n\t\theight).  Reduces the current window height to create room\n\t\t(and others, if the 'equalalways' option is set).\n\nCTRL-W CTRL-V\t\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_CTRL-V*\nCTRL-W v\t\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_v*\n:[N]vs[plit] [++opt] [+cmd] [file]\t\t\t*:vs* *:vsplit*\n\t\tLike |:split|, but split vertically.  The windows will be\n\t\tspread out horizontally if\n\t\t1. a width was not specified,\n\t\t2. 'equalalways' is set,\n\t\t3. 'eadirection' isn't \"ver\", and\n\t\t4. one of the other windows is wider than the current or new\n\t\t   window.\n\t\tIf N was given make the new window N columns wide, if\n\t\tpossible.\n\t\tNote: In other places CTRL-Q does the same as CTRL-V, but here\n\t\tit doesn't!\n\nCTRL-W n\t\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_n*\nCTRL-W CTRL-N\t\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_CTRL-N*\n:[N]new [++opt] [+cmd]\t\t\t\t\t*:new*\n\t\tCreate a new window and start editing an empty file in it.\n\t\tMake new window N high (default is to use half the existing\n\t\theight).  Reduces the current window height to create room\n\t\t(and others, if the 'equalalways' option is set and\n\t\t'eadirection' isn't \"hor\").\n\t\tAlso see |++opt| and |+cmd|.\n\t\tIf 'fileformats' is not empty, the first format given will be\n\t\tused for the new buffer.  If 'fileformats' is empty, the\n\t\t'fileformat' of the current buffer is used.  This can be\n\t\toverridden with the |++opt| argument.\n\t\tAutocommands are executed in this order:\n\t\t1. WinLeave for the current window\n\t\t2. WinEnter for the new window\n\t\t3. BufLeave for the current buffer\n\t\t4. BufEnter for the new buffer\n\t\tThis behaves like a \":split\" first, and then an \":enew\"\n\t\tcommand.\n\n:[N]new [++opt] [+cmd] {file}\n\t\tLike |:split_f|, create a new window and start editing {file}.\n\n:[N]vne[w] [++opt] [+cmd] [file]\t\t\t*:vne* *:vnew*\n\t\tLike |:new|, but split vertically.  If 'equalalways' is set\n\t\tand 'eadirection' isn't \"ver\" the windows will be spread out\n\t\thorizontally, unless a width was specified.\n\n:[N]sv[iew] [++opt] [+cmd] [file]\t\t*:sv* *:sview* *splitview*\n\t\tSame as \":split\", but set 'readonly' option for this buffer.\n\n:[N]sf[ind] [++opt] [+cmd] {file}\t     *:sf* *:sfi* *:sfind* *splitfind*\n\t\tSame as \":split\", but search for {file} in 'path' like in\n\t\t|:find|.  Doesn't split if {file} is not found.\n\nCTRL-W CTRL-^\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_CTRL-^* *CTRL-W_^*\nCTRL-W ^\tSplit the current window in two and edit the alternate file.\n\t\tWhen a count N is given, split the current window and edit\n\t\tbuffer N.  Similar to \":sp #\" and \":sp #N\", but it allows the\n\t\tother buffer to be unnamed.  This command matches the behavior\n\t\tof |CTRL-^|, except that it splits a window first.\n\nCTRL-W ge\t\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_ge*\n\t\tDetach the current window as an external window.\n\t\tOnly available when using a UI with |ui-multigrid| support.\n\nNote that the 'splitbelow' and 'splitright' options influence where a new\nwindow will appear.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t*E36*\nCreating a window will fail if there is not enough room.  Every window needs\nat least one screen line and column, sometimes more.   Options 'winminheight'\nand 'winminwidth' are relevant.\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t*:vert* *:vertical*\n:vert[ical] {cmd}\n\t\tExecute {cmd}.  If it contains a command that splits a window,\n\t\tit will be split vertically.  For `vertical wincmd =` windows\n\t\twill be equalized only vertically.\n\t\tDoesn't work for |:execute| and |:normal|.\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t*:hor* *:horizontal*\n:hor[izontal] {cmd}\n\t\tExecute {cmd} in a horizontal split window. Supports these\n\t\tcommands:\n\t\t- `:wincmd =`: equalize windows only horizontally.\n\t\t- |:terminal|: open a |terminal| buffer in a split window.\n\t\t- |:checkhealth|: open a healthcheck buffer in a split window.\n\n:lefta[bove] {cmd}\t\t\t\t*:lefta* *:leftabove*\n:abo[veleft] {cmd}\t\t\t\t*:abo* *:aboveleft*\n\t\tExecute {cmd}.  If it contains a command that splits a window,\n\t\tit will be opened left (vertical split) or above (horizontal\n\t\tsplit) the current window.  Overrules 'splitbelow' and\n\t\t'splitright'.\n\t\tDoesn't work for |:execute| and |:normal|.\n\n:rightb[elow] {cmd}\t\t\t\t*:rightb* *:rightbelow*\n:bel[owright] {cmd}\t\t\t\t*:bel* *:belowright*\n\t\tExecute {cmd}.  If it contains a command that splits a window,\n\t\tit will be opened right (vertical split) or below (horizontal\n\t\tsplit) the current window.  Overrules 'splitbelow' and\n\t\t'splitright'.\n\t\tDoesn't work for |:execute| and |:normal|.\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t*:topleft* *E442*\n:to[pleft] {cmd}\n\t\tExecute {cmd}.  If it contains a command that splits a window,\n\t\tit will appear at the top and occupy the full width of the Vim\n\t\twindow.  When the split is vertical the window appears at the\n\t\tfar left and occupies the full height of the Vim window.\n\t\tDoesn't work for |:execute| and |:normal|.\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t*:bo* *:botright*\n:bo[tright] {cmd}\n\t\tExecute {cmd}.  If it contains a command that splits a window,\n\t\tit will appear at the bottom and occupy the full width of the\n\t\tVim window.  When the split is vertical the window appears at\n\t\tthe far right and occupies the full height of the Vim window.\n\t\tDoesn't work for |:execute| and |:normal|.\n\nThese command modifiers can be combined to make a vertically split window\noccupy the full height.  Example: >\n\t:vertical topleft split tags\nOpens a vertically split, full-height window on the \"tags\" file at the far\nleft of the Vim window.\n\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------\nClosing a window\n\n:q[uit]\n:{count}q[uit]\t\t\t\t\t\t*:count_quit*\nCTRL-W q\t\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_q*\nCTRL-W CTRL-Q\t\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_CTRL-Q*\n\t\tWithout {count}: Quit the current window.  If {count} is\n\t\tgiven quit the {count} window.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t*edit-window*\n\t\tWhen quitting the last edit window (not counting help or\n\t\tpreview windows), exit Vim.\n\n\t\tWhen 'hidden' is set, and there is only one window for the\n\t\tcurrent buffer, it becomes hidden. When 'hidden' is not set,\n\t\tand there is only one window for the current buffer, and the\n\t\tbuffer was changed, the command fails.\n\t\t(Note: CTRL-Q does not work on all terminals).\n\t\tIf [count] is greater than the last window number the last\n\t\twindow will be closed: >\n\t\t    :1quit  \" quit the first window\n\t\t    :$quit  \" quit the last window\n\t\t    :9quit  \" quit the last window\n\t\t\t    \" if there are fewer than 9 windows opened\n\t\t    :-quit  \" quit the previous window\n\t\t    :+quit  \" quit the next window\n\t\t    :+2quit \" quit the second next window\n<\n\t\tWhen closing a help window, and this is not the only window,\n\t\tVim will try to restore the previous window layout, see\n\t\t|:helpclose|.\n\n:q[uit]!\n:{count}q[uit]!\n\t\tWithout {count}: Quit the current window.  If {count} is\n\t\tgiven quit the {count} window\n\t\tIf this was the last window for a buffer, any changes to that\n\t\tbuffer are lost. When quitting the last window (not counting\n\t\thelp windows), exit Vim. The contents of the buffer are lost,\n\t\teven when 'hidden' is set.\n\n:clo[se][!]\n:{count}clo[se][!]\nCTRL-W c\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_c* *:clo* *:close*\n\t\tWithout {count}: Close the current window. If given close the\n\t\t{count} window.\n\n\t\tWhen 'hidden' is set, or when the buffer was changed and the\n\t\t[!] is used, the buffer becomes hidden (unless there is another\n\t\twindow editing it).\n\n\t\tWhen there is only one |edit-window| in the current |tabpage|\n\t\tand there is another tabpage, this closes the current tabpage.\n\n\t\tThis command fails when:\t\t\t*E444*\n\t\t- There is only one window on the screen.\n\t\t- When 'hidden' is not set, [!] is not used, the buffer has\n\t\t  changes, and there is no other window on this buffer.\n\t\tChanges to the buffer are not written and won't get lost, so\n\t\tthis is a \"safe\" command.\n\nCTRL-W CTRL-C\t\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_CTRL-C*\n\t\tYou might have expected that CTRL-W CTRL-C closes the current\n\t\twindow, but that does not work, because the CTRL-C cancels the\n\t\tcommand.\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t*:hide*\n:hid[e]\n:{count}hid[e]\n\t\tWithout {count}: Quit the current window, unless it is the\n\t\tlast window on the screen.\n\t\tIf {count} is given quit the {count} window.\n\n\t\tThe buffer becomes hidden (unless there is another window\n\t\tediting it or 'bufhidden' is `unload`, `delete` or `wipe`).\n\t\tIf the window is the last one in the current |tabpage| the\n\t\ttabpage is closed.\n\n\t\tThe value of 'hidden' is irrelevant for this command.\n\t\tChanges to the buffer are not written and won't get lost, so\n\t\tthis is a \"safe\" command.\n\n:hid[e] {cmd}\tExecute {cmd} with 'hidden' set. The previous value of\n\t\t'hidden' is restored after {cmd} has been executed.\n\t\tExample: >\n\t\t    :hide edit Makefile\n<\t\tThis will edit \"Makefile\", and hide the current buffer if it\n\t\thas any changes.\n\n:on[ly][!]\n:{count}on[ly][!]\nCTRL-W o\t\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_o* *E445*\nCTRL-W CTRL-O\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_CTRL-O* *:on* *:only*\n\t\tMake the current window the only one on the screen. All other\n\t\twindows are closed.  For {count} see the `:quit` command\n\t\tabove |:count_quit|.\n\n\t\tWhen the 'hidden' option is set, all buffers in closed windows\n\t\tbecome hidden.\n\n\t\tWhen 'hidden' is not set, and the 'autowrite' option is set,\n\t\tmodified buffers are written.  Otherwise, windows that have\n\t\tbuffers that are modified are not removed, unless the [!] is\n\t\tgiven, then they become hidden.  But modified buffers are\n\t\tnever abandoned, so changes cannot get lost.\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t*:fc* *:fclose*\n:[count]fc[lose][!]\n\t\tClose [count] floating windows with the highest zindex values.\n\t\t'!' to close all floating windows.\n\n==============================================================================\n4. Moving cursor to other windows\t\t\t*window-move-cursor*\n\nCTRL-W <Down>\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_<Down>*\nCTRL-W CTRL-J\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_CTRL-J* *CTRL-W_j*\nCTRL-W j\tMove cursor to Nth window below current one.  Uses the cursor\n\t\tposition to select between alternatives.\n\nCTRL-W <Up>\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_<Up>*\nCTRL-W CTRL-K\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_CTRL-K* *CTRL-W_k*\nCTRL-W k\tMove cursor to Nth window above current one.  Uses the cursor\n\t\tposition to select between alternatives.\n\nCTRL-W <Left>\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_<Left>*\nCTRL-W CTRL-H\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_CTRL-H*\nCTRL-W <BS>\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_<BS>* *CTRL-W_h*\nCTRL-W h\tMove cursor to Nth window left of current one.  Uses the\n\t\tcursor position to select between alternatives.\n\nCTRL-W <Right>\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_<Right>*\nCTRL-W CTRL-L\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_CTRL-L* *CTRL-W_l*\nCTRL-W l\tMove cursor to Nth window right of current one.  Uses the\n\t\tcursor position to select between alternatives.\n\nCTRL-W w\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_w* *CTRL-W_CTRL-W*\nCTRL-W CTRL-W\tWithout count: move cursor to the |focusable| window\n\t\tbelow/right of the current one.  If none, go to the top-left\n\t\twindow.  With count: go to Nth window (numbered top-left to\n\t\tbottom-right), skipping unfocusable windows.  To obtain the\n\t\twindow number see |bufwinnr()| and |winnr()|.  When N is\n\t\tlarger than the number of windows go to the last focusable\n\t\twindow.\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_W*\nCTRL-W W\tWithout count: move cursor to the |focusable| window\n\t\tabove/left of current one.  If none, go to the bottom-right\n\t\twindow.  With count: go to Nth window, like CTRL-W w.\n\nCTRL-W t\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_t* *CTRL-W_CTRL-T*\nCTRL-W CTRL-T\tMove cursor to top-left window.\n\nCTRL-W b\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_b* *CTRL-W_CTRL-B*\nCTRL-W CTRL-B\tMove cursor to bottom-right window.\n\nCTRL-W p\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_p* *CTRL-W_CTRL-P*\nCTRL-W CTRL-P\tGo to previous (last accessed) window.\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_P* *E441*\nCTRL-W P\tGo to preview window.  When there is no preview window this is\n\t\tan error.\n\nIf Visual mode is active and the new window is not for the same buffer, the\nVisual mode is ended.  If the window is on the same buffer, the cursor\nposition is set to keep the same Visual area selected.\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t*:winc* *:wincmd*\nThese commands can also be executed with \":wincmd\":\n\n:[count]winc[md] {arg}\n:winc[md] [count] {arg}\n\t\tLike executing CTRL-W [count] {arg}.  Example: >\n\t\t\t:wincmd j\n<\t\tMoves to the window below the current one.\n\t\tThis command is useful when a Normal mode cannot be used (for\n\t\tthe |CursorHold| autocommand event).  Or when a Normal mode\n\t\tcommand is inconvenient.\n\t\tThe count can also be a window number.  Example: >\n\t\t\t:exe nr .. \"wincmd w\"\n<\t\tThis goes to window \"nr\".\n\nNote: All CTRL-W commands can also be executed with |:wincmd|, for those\nplaces where a Normal mode command can't be used or is inconvenient (e.g.\nin a browser-based terminal).\n\n==============================================================================\n5. Moving windows around\t\t\t\t*window-moving*\n\nCTRL-W r\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_r* *CTRL-W_CTRL-R* *E443*\nCTRL-W CTRL-R\tRotate windows downwards/rightwards.  The first window becomes\n\t\tthe second one, the second one becomes the third one, etc.\n\t\tThe last window becomes the first window.  The cursor remains\n\t\tin the same window.\n\t\tThis only works within the row or column of windows that the\n\t\tcurrent window is in.\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_R*\nCTRL-W R\tRotate windows upwards/leftwards.  The second window becomes\n\t\tthe first one, the third one becomes the second one, etc.  The\n\t\tfirst window becomes the last window.  The cursor remains in\n\t\tthe same window.\n\t\tThis only works within the row or column of windows that the\n\t\tcurrent window is in.\n\nCTRL-W x\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_x* *CTRL-W_CTRL-X*\nCTRL-W CTRL-X\tWithout count: Exchange current window with next one.  If\n\t\tthere is no next window, exchange with previous window.\n\t\tWith count: Exchange current window with Nth window (first\n\t\twindow is 1).  The cursor is put in the other window.\n\t\tWhen vertical and horizontal window splits are mixed, the\n\t\texchange is only done in the row or column of windows that the\n\t\tcurrent window is in.\n\nThe following commands can be used to change the window layout.  For example,\nwhen there are two vertically split windows, CTRL-W K will change that in\nhorizontally split windows.  CTRL-W H does it the other way around.\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_K*\nCTRL-W K\tMove the current window to be at the very top, using the full\n\t\twidth of the screen.  This works like `:topleft split`, except\n\t\tit is applied to the current window and no new window is\n\t\tcreated.\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_J*\nCTRL-W J\tMove the current window to be at the very bottom, using the\n\t\tfull width of the screen.  This works like `:botright split`,\n\t\texcept it is applied to the current window and no new window\n\t\tis created.\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_H*\nCTRL-W H\tMove the current window to be at the far left, using the\n\t\tfull height of the screen.  This works like\n\t\t`:vert topleft split`, except it is applied to the current\n\t\twindow and no new window is created.\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_L*\nCTRL-W L\tMove the current window to be at the far right, using the full\n\t\theight of the screen.  This works like `:vert botright split`,\n\t\texcept it is applied to the current window and no new window\n\t\tis created.\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_T*\nCTRL-W T\tMove the current window to a new tabpage.  This fails if\n\t\tthere is only one window in the current tabpage.\n\t\tThis works like `:tab split`, except the previous window is\n\t\tclosed.\n\t\tWhen a count is specified the new tabpage will be opened\n\t\tbefore the tabpage with this index.  Otherwise it comes after\n\t\tthe current tabpage.\n\n==============================================================================\n6. Window resizing\t\t\t\t\t*window-resize*\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_=*\nCTRL-W =\tMake all windows (almost) equally high and wide, but use\n\t\t'winheight' and 'winwidth' for the current window. Windows\n\t\twith 'winfixheight' set keep their height, and windows with\n\t\t'winfixwidth' set keep their width.\n\n\t\tTo equalize only vertically (each window equally high) use: >\n\t\t    :vertical wincmd =\n<\n\t\tTo equalize only horizontally (each window equally wide) use: >\n\t\t    :horizontal wincmd =\n<\n\t\tTo equalize windows when Nvim itself is resized, see\n\t\t|VimResized|.\n\n:res[ize] -N\t\t\t\t\t*:res* *:resize* *CTRL-W_-*\nCTRL-W -\tDecrease current window height by N (default 1).\n\t\tIf used after |:vertical|: decrease width by N.\n\n:res[ize] +N\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_+*\nCTRL-W +\tIncrease current window height by N (default 1).\n\t\tIf used after |:vertical|: increase width by N.\n\n:res[ize] [N]\nCTRL-W CTRL-_\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_CTRL-_* *CTRL-W__*\nCTRL-W _\tSet current window height to N (default: highest possible).\n\n:{winnr}res[ize] [+-]N\n\t\tLike `:resize` above, but apply the size to window {winnr}\n\t\tinstead of the current window. See also |nvim_win_resize()|.\n\nz{nr}<CR>\tSet current window height to {nr}.\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_<*\nCTRL-W <\tDecrease current window width by N (default 1).\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_>*\nCTRL-W >\tIncrease current window width by N (default 1).\n\n:vert[ical] res[ize] [N]\t\t\t*:vertical-resize* *CTRL-W_bar*\nCTRL-W |\tSet current window width to N (default: widest possible).\n\nYou can also resize a window by dragging a status line up or down with the\nmouse.  Or by dragging a vertical separator line left or right.  This only\nworks if the version of Vim that is being used supports the mouse and the\n'mouse' option has been set to enable it.\n\nThe option 'winheight' ('wh') is used to set the minimal window height of the\ncurrent window.  This option is used each time another window becomes the\ncurrent window.  If the option is '0', it is disabled.  Set 'winheight' to a\nvery large value, e.g., '9999', to make the current window always fill all\navailable space.  Set it to a reasonable value, e.g., '10', to make editing in\nthe current window comfortable.\n\nThe equivalent 'winwidth' ('wiw') option is used to set the minimal width of\nthe current window.\n\nWhen the option 'equalalways' ('ea') is set, all the windows are automatically\nmade the same size after splitting or closing a window.  If you don't set this\noption, splitting a window will reduce the size of the current window and\nleave the other windows the same.  When closing a window, the extra lines are\ngiven to the window above it.\n\nThe 'eadirection' option limits the direction in which the 'equalalways'\noption is applied.  The default \"both\" resizes in both directions.  When the\nvalue is \"ver\" only the heights of windows are equalized.  Use this when you\nhave manually resized a vertically split window and want to keep this width.\nLikewise, \"hor\" causes only the widths of windows to be equalized.\n\nThe option 'cmdheight' ('ch') is used to set the height of the command-line.\nIf you are annoyed by the |hit-enter| prompt for long messages, set this\noption to 2 or 3.\n\nIf there is only one window, resizing that window will also change the command\nline height.  If there are several windows, resizing the current window will\nalso change the height of the window below it (and sometimes the window above\nit).\n\nThe minimal height and width of a window is set with 'winminheight' and\n'winminwidth'.  These are hard values, a window will never become smaller.\n\n\nWinScrolled and WinResized autocommands ~\n\t\t\t\t\t\t*win-scrolled-resized*\nIf you want to get notified of changes in window sizes, the |WinResized|\nautocommand event can be used.\nIf you want to get notified of text in windows scrolling vertically or\nhorizontally, the |WinScrolled| autocommand event can be used.  This will also\ntrigger in window size changes.\nException: the events will not be triggered when the text scrolls for\n'incsearch'.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t*WinResized-event*\nThe |WinResized| event is triggered after updating the display, several\nwindows may have changed size then.  A list of the IDs of windows that changed\nsince last time is provided in the v:event.windows variable, for example:\n\t[1003, 1006]\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t*WinScrolled-event*\nThe |WinScrolled| event is triggered after |WinResized|, and also if a window\nwas scrolled.  That can be vertically (the text at the top of the window\nchanged) or horizontally (when 'wrap' is off or when the first displayed part\nof the first line changes).  Note that |WinScrolled| will trigger many more\ntimes than |WinResized|, it may slow down editing a bit.\n\nThe information provided by |WinScrolled| is a dictionary for each window that\nhas changes, using the window ID as the key, and a total count of the changes\nwith the key \"all\".  Example value for |v:event|: >\n\t{\n\t   all:  {width: 0, height:  2, leftcol: 0, skipcol: 0, topline: 1, topfill: 0},\n\t   1003: {width: 0, height: -1, leftcol: 0, skipcol: 0, topline: 0, topfill: 0},\n\t   1006: {width: 0, height:  1, leftcol: 0, skipcol: 0, topline: 1, topfill: 0},\n\t}\n\nNote that the \"all\" entry has the absolute values of the individual windows\naccumulated.\n\nIf you need more information about what changed, or you want to \"debounce\" the\nevents (not handle every event to avoid doing too much work), you may want to\nuse the `winlayout()` and `getwininfo()` functions.\n\n|WinScrolled| and |WinResized| do not trigger when the first autocommand is\nadded, only after the first scroll or resize.  They may trigger when switching\nto another tabpage.\n\nThe commands executed are expected to not cause window size or scroll changes.\nIf this happens anyway, the event will trigger again very soon.  In other\nwords: Just before triggering the event, the current sizes and scroll\npositions are stored and used to decide whether there was a change.\n\n==============================================================================\n7. compatibility with Vi.\n\n\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------\nThe argument list and multiple windows\n\nThe current position in the argument list can be different for each window.\nRemember that when doing \":e file\", the position in the argument list stays\nthe same, but you are not editing the file at that position.  To indicate\nthis, the file message (and the title, if you have one) shows\n\"(file (N) of M)\", where \"(N)\" is the current position in the file list, and\n\"M\" the number of files in the file list.\n\nAll the entries in the argument list are added to the buffer list.  Thus, you\ncan also get to them with the buffer list commands, like \":bnext\".\n\n:[N]al[l][!] [N]\t\t\t\t*:al* *:all* *:sal* *:sall*\n:[N]sal[l][!] [N]\n\t\tRearrange the screen to open one window for each argument.\n\t\tAll other windows are closed.  When a count is given, this is\n\t\tthe maximum number of windows to open.\n\t\tWith the |:tab| modifier open a tabpage for each argument.\n\t\tWhen there are more arguments than 'tabpagemax' further ones\n\t\tbecome split windows in the last tabpage.\n\t\tWhen the 'hidden' option is set, all buffers in closed windows\n\t\tbecome hidden.\n\t\tWhen 'hidden' is not set, and the 'autowrite' option is set,\n\t\tmodified buffers are written.  Otherwise, windows that have\n\t\tbuffers that are modified are not removed, unless the [!] is\n\t\tgiven, then they become hidden.  But modified buffers are\n\t\tnever abandoned, so changes cannot get lost.\n\t\t[N] is the maximum number of windows to open.  'winheight'\n\t\talso limits the number of windows opened ('winwidth' if\n\t\t|:vertical| was prepended).\n\t\tBuf/Win Enter/Leave autocommands are not executed for the new\n\t\twindows here, that's only done when they are really entered.\n\t\tIf autocommands change the window layout while this command is\n\t\tbusy an error will be given. *E249*\n\n:[N]sa[rgument][!] [++opt] [+cmd] [N]\t\t\t*:sa* *:sargument*\n\t\tShort for \":split | argument [N]\": split window and go to Nth\n\t\targument.  But when there is no such argument, the window is\n\t\tnot split.  Also see |++opt| and |+cmd|.\n\n:[N]sn[ext][!] [++opt] [+cmd] [file ..]\t\t\t*:sn* *:snext*\n\t\tShort for \":split | [N]next\": split window and go to Nth next\n\t\targument.  But when there is no next file, the window is not\n\t\tsplit.  Also see |++opt| and |+cmd|.\n\n:[N]spr[evious][!] [++opt] [+cmd] [N]\t\t\t*:spr* *:sprevious*\n:[N]sN[ext][!] [++opt] [+cmd] [N]\t\t\t*:sN* *:sNext*\n\t\tShort for \":split | [N]Next\": split window and go to Nth\n\t\tprevious argument.  But when there is no previous file, the\n\t\twindow is not split.  Also see |++opt| and |+cmd|.\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t*:sre* *:srewind*\n:sre[wind][!] [++opt] [+cmd]\n\t\tShort for \":split | rewind\": split window and go to first\n\t\targument.  But when there is no argument list, the window is\n\t\tnot split.  Also see |++opt| and |+cmd|.\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t*:sfir* *:sfirst*\n:sfir[st] [++opt] [+cmd]\n\t\tSame as \":srewind\".\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t*:sla* *:slast*\n:sla[st][!] [++opt] [+cmd]\n\t\tShort for \":split | last\": split window and go to last\n\t\targument.  But when there is no argument list, the window is\n\t\tnot split.  Also see |++opt| and |+cmd|.\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t*:dr* *:drop*\n:dr[op] [++opt] [+cmd] {file} ..\n\t\tEdit the first {file} in a window.\n\t\t- If the file is already open in a window change to that\n\t\t  window.\n\t\t- If the file is not open in a window edit the file in the\n\t\t  current window.  If the current buffer can't be |abandon|ed,\n\t\t  the window is split first.\n\t\t- Windows that are not in the argument list or are not full\n\t\t  width will be closed if possible.\n\t\tThe |argument-list| is set, like with the |:next| command.\n\t\tThe purpose of this command is that it can be used from a\n\t\tprogram that wants Vim to edit another file, e.g., a debugger.\n\t\tWhen using the |:tab| modifier each argument is opened in a\n\t\ttabpage.  The last window is used if it's empty.\n\t\tAlso see |++opt| and |+cmd|.\n\n==============================================================================\n8. Do a command in all buffers or windows\t\t\t*list-repeat*\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t*:windo*\n:[range]windo {cmd}\tExecute {cmd} in each |focusable| window, or only for\n\t\t\twindows in a given [range] of window numbers. It works\n\t\t\tlike doing this: >\n\t\t\t\tCTRL-W t\n\t\t\t\t:{cmd}\n\t\t\t\tCTRL-W w\n\t\t\t\t:{cmd}\n\t\t\t\tetc.\n<\t\t\tThis only operates in the current tabpage.\n\t\t\tWhen an error is detected on one window, further\n\t\t\twindows will not be visited.\n\t\t\tThe last window (or where an error occurred) becomes\n\t\t\tthe current window.\n\t\t\t{cmd} can contain '|' to concatenate several commands.\n\t\t\t{cmd} must not open or close windows or reorder them.\n\n\t\t\tAlso see |:tabdo|, |:argdo|, |:bufdo|, |:cdo|, |:ldo|,\n\t\t\t|:cfdo| and |:lfdo|.\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t*:bufdo*\n:[range]bufdo[!] {cmd}\tExecute {cmd} in each buffer in the buffer list or if\n\t\t\t[range] is given only for buffers for which their\n\t\t\tbuffer number is in the [range]. It works like doing\n\t\t\tthis: >\n\t\t\t\t:bfirst\n\t\t\t\t:{cmd}\n\t\t\t\t:bnext\n\t\t\t\t:{cmd}\n\t\t\t\tetc.\n<\t\t\tWhen the current file can't be |abandon|ed and the [!]\n\t\t\tis not present, the command fails.\n\t\t\tWhen an error is detected on one buffer, further\n\t\t\tbuffers will not be visited.\n\t\t\tUnlisted buffers are skipped.\n\t\t\tThe last buffer (or where an error occurred) becomes\n\t\t\tthe current buffer.\n\t\t\t{cmd} can contain '|' to concatenate several commands.\n\t\t\t{cmd} must not delete buffers or add buffers to the\n\t\t\tbuffer list.\n\t\t\tNote: While this command is executing, the Syntax\n\t\t\tautocommand event is disabled by adding it to\n\t\t\t'eventignore'.  This considerably speeds up editing\n\t\t\teach buffer.\n\n\t\t\tAlso see |:tabdo|, |:argdo|, |:windo|, |:cdo|, |:ldo|,\n\t\t\t|:cfdo| and |:lfdo|.\n\nExamples: >\n\n\t:windo set nolist foldcolumn=0 | normal! zn\n\nThis resets the 'list' option and disables folding in all windows. >\n\n\t:bufdo set fileencoding= | update\n\nThis resets the 'fileencoding' in each buffer and writes it if this changed\nthe buffer.  The result is that all buffers will use the 'encoding' encoding\n(if conversion succeeds).\n\n==============================================================================\n9. Tag or file name under the cursor\t\t\t*window-tag*\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t*:sta* *:stag*\n:sta[g][!] [tagname]\n\t\tDoes \":tag[!] [tagname]\" and splits the window for the found\n\t\ttag.  Refer to 'switchbuf' to jump to a tag in a vertically\n\t\tsplit window or a new tabpage.  See also |:tag|.\n\nCTRL-W ]\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_]* *CTRL-W_CTRL-]*\nCTRL-W CTRL-]\tSplit current window in two.  Use identifier under cursor as a\n\t\ttag and jump to it in the new upper window.\n\t\tIn Visual mode uses the Visually selected text as a tag.\n\t\tMake new window N high.  Refer to 'switchbuf' to jump to a tag\n\t\tin a vertically split window or a new tabpage.\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_g]*\nCTRL-W g ]\tSplit current window in two.  Use identifier under cursor as a\n\t\ttag and perform \":tselect\" on it in the new upper window.\n\t\tIn Visual mode uses the Visually selected text as a tag.\n\t\tMake new window N high.\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_g_CTRL-]*\nCTRL-W g CTRL-]\tSplit current window in two.  Use identifier under cursor as a\n\t\ttag and perform \":tjump\" on it in the new upper window.\n\t\tIn Visual mode uses the Visually selected text as a tag.\n\t\tMake new window N high.\n\nCTRL-W f\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_f* *CTRL-W_CTRL-F*\nCTRL-W CTRL-F\tSplit current window in two.  Edit file name under cursor.\n\t\tLike \":split gf\", but window isn't split if the file does not\n\t\texist.\n\t\tUses the 'path' variable as a list of directory names where to\n\t\tlook for the file.  Also the path for current file is\n\t\tused to search for the file name.\n\t\tIf the name is a hypertext link that looks like\n\t\t\"type://machine/path\", only \"/path\" is used.\n\t\tIf a count is given, the count'th matching file is edited.\n\nCTRL-W F\t\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_F*\n\t\tSplit current window in two.  Edit file name under cursor and\n\t\tjump to the line number following the file name.  See |gF| for\n\t\tdetails on how the line number is obtained.\n\nCTRL-W gf\t\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_gf*\n\t\tOpen a new tabpage and edit the file name under the cursor.\n\t\tLike \"tab split\" and \"gf\", but the new tabpage isn't created\n\t\tif the file does not exist.\n\nCTRL-W gF\t\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_gF*\n\t\tOpen a new tabpage and edit the file name under the cursor\n\t\tand jump to the line number following the file name.  Like\n\t\t\"tab split\" and \"gF\", but the new tabpage isn't created if\n\t\tthe file does not exist.\n\nCTRL-W gt\t\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_gt*\n\t\tGo to next tabpage, same as `gt`.\n\nCTRL-W gT\t\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_gT*\n\t\tGo to previous tabpage, same as `gT`.\n\nAlso see |CTRL-W_CTRL-I|: open window for an included file that includes\nthe keyword under the cursor.\n\n==============================================================================\n10. The preview window\t\t\t\t*preview-window*\n\nThe preview window is a special window to show (preview) another file.  It is\nnormally a small window used to show an include file or definition of a\nfunction.\n\nThere can be only one preview window (per tabpage).  It is created with one\nof the commands below.  The 'previewheight' option can be set to specify the\nheight of the preview window when it's opened.  The 'previewwindow' option is\nset in the preview window to be able to recognize it.  The 'winfixheight'\noption is set to have it keep the same height when opening/closing other\nwindows.\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t*preview-popup*\nAlternatively, a floating window can be used by setting the 'previewpopup'\noption.  When set, it overrules the 'previewwindow' and 'previewheight'\nsettings.\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t*:pt* *:ptag*\n:pt[ag][!] [tagname]\n\t\tDoes \":tag[!] [tagname]\" and shows the found tag in a\n\t\t\"Preview\" window without changing the current buffer or cursor\n\t\tposition.  If a \"Preview\" window already exists, it is re-used\n\t\t(like a help window is).  If a new one is opened,\n\t\t'previewheight' is used for the height of the window.   See\n\t\talso |:tag|.\n\t\tSee below for an example. |CursorHold-example|\n\t\tSmall difference from |:tag|: When [tagname] is equal to the\n\t\talready displayed tag, the position in the matching tag list\n\t\tis not reset.  This makes the CursorHold example work after a\n\t\t|:ptnext|.\n\nCTRL-W z\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_z*\nCTRL-W CTRL-Z\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_CTRL-Z* *:pc* *:pclose*\n:pc[lose][!]\tClose any \"Preview\" window currently open.  When the 'hidden'\n\t\toption is set, or when the buffer was changed and the [!] is\n\t\tused, the buffer becomes hidden (unless there is another\n\t\twindow editing it).  The command fails if any \"Preview\" buffer\n\t\tcannot be closed.  See also |:close|.\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t*:pp* *:ppop*\n:[count]pp[op][!]\n\t\tDoes \":[count]pop[!]\" in the preview window.  See |:pop| and\n\t\t|:ptag|.\n\nCTRL-W }\t\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_}*\n\t\tUse identifier under cursor as a tag and perform a :ptag on\n\t\tit.  Make the new Preview window (if required) N high.  If N\n\t\tis not given, 'previewheight' is used.\n\nCTRL-W g }\t\t\t\t\t\t*CTRL-W_g}*\n\t\tUse identifier under cursor as a tag and perform a :ptjump on\n\t\tit.  Make the new Preview window (if required) N high.  If N\n\t\tis not given, 'previewheight' is used.\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t*:pb* *:pbuffer*\n:[N]pb[uffer][!] [+cmd] [N]\n\t\tEdit buffer [N] from the buffer list in the preview window.\n\t\tIf [N] is not given, the current buffer remains being edited.\n\t\tSee |:buffer-!| for [!].  This will also edit a buffer that is\n\t\tnot in the buffer list, without setting the 'buflisted' flag.\n\t\tAlso see |+cmd|.\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t*:ped* *:pedit*\n:ped[it][!] [++opt] [+cmd] {file}\n\t\tEdit {file} in the preview window.  The preview window is\n\t\topened like with |:ptag|.  The current window and cursor\n\t\tposition isn't changed.  Useful example: >\n\t\t\t:pedit +/fputc /usr/include/stdio.h\n<\n\t\tAlso see |++opt| and |+cmd|.\n\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t*:ps* *:psearch*\n:[range]ps[earch][!] [count] [/]pattern[/]\n\t\tWorks like |:ijump| but shows the found match in the preview\n\t\twindow.  The preview window is opened like with |:ptag|.  The\n\t\tcurrent window and cursor position isn't changed.  Useful\n\t\texample: >\n\t\t\t:psearch popen\n<\t\tLike with the |:ptag| command, you can use this to\n\t\tautomatically show information about the word under the\n\t\tcursor.  This is less clever than using |:ptag|, but you don't\n\t\tneed a tags file and it will also find matches in system\n\t\tinclude files.  Example: >\n  :au! CursorHold *.[ch] ++nested exe \"silent! psearch \" .. expand(\"<cword>\")\n<\t\tWarning: This can be slow.\n\nExample\t\t\t\t\t\t*CursorHold-example*  >\n\n  :au! CursorHold *.[ch] ++nested exe \"silent! ptag \" .. expand(\"<cword>\")\n\nThis will cause a \":ptag\" to be executed for the keyword under the cursor,\nwhen the cursor hasn't moved for the time set with 'updatetime'.  \"++nested\"\nmakes other autocommands be executed, so that syntax highlighting works in the\npreview window. ---@field embedding_dimension integer @Dimensionality of the model's embedding space
---@field parameter_count integer @Total number of parameters in the model
---@field model_size_bytes integer @Size of the model file in bytes

local ModelInfo = {}
ModelInfo.__index = ModelInfo

---@param id string
---@param aliases string[]
---@param created integer
---@param owned_by string
---@param meta table @Raw meta table from the API response
---@return ModelInfo
function ModelInfo:new(id, aliases, created, owned_by, meta)
    local obj = {
        name = id,
        alias = #aliases > 0 and aliases[1] or "",
        created = created,
        owned_by = owned_by,
        vocabulary_size = meta.n_vocab or 0,
        context_length = meta.n_ctx or 0,
        context_length_train = meta.n_ctx_train or 0,
        embedding_dimension = meta.n_embd or 0,
        parameter_count = meta.n_params or 0,
        model_size_bytes = meta.size or 0,
    }
    setmetatable(obj, ModelInfo)
    return obj
end

---@param url string
---@param method Methods
---@param request_body? table
---@param opts? HttpTimeoutOptions @optional timeout configuration (nil = no timeout)
---@return JsonClientResponse?
function JsonClient.get_response_body(url, method, request_body, opts)
    local request_json = nil
    if request_body then

        "-X", method,

    }

    if opts then
        if opts.connect_timeout then
            table.insert(curl_args, "--connect-timeout")
            table.insert(curl_args, tostring(opts.connect_timeout))
        end
        if opts.max_time then
            table.insert(curl_args, "--max-time")

        end
    end

    if request_json then
        table.insert(curl_args, "-d")
        table.insert(curl_args, request_json)
    end

    table.insert(curl_args, url)

---@field _last_start number

local Timer = {}

local function get_now_in_nanoseconds_counter()
    if host.is_hammerspoon() then
        -- hs.timer.absoluteTime() returns nanoseconds
        return hs.timer.absoluteTime() / 1e9
    else
        local uv = vim.uv or vim.loop

    end

--- devtools.notify
---
--- A deliberately simple notification module.
---
--- Notifications are shown as a plain box in the top-right corner of the
--- editor and disappear on their own after a timeout. No animations, no
--- window management tricks, no "features". Just a message you can read and
--- a box that goes away.
---
--- Usage:
---   local notify = require("devtools.notify")
---   notify.info("Model is loaded", { title = "AskAgentCheckModel", timeout = 5000 })
---   notify.notify("boom", vim.log.levels.ERROR, { title = "Oops" })

local M = {}

local config = {
    timeout_ms = 5000,   -- default time a notification stays up
    border = "single",   -- border style: "single" | "rounded" | "none"
    margin_top = 1,      -- rows from the top of the editor
    margin_right = 1,    -- cols from the right edge of the editor
    gap = 1,             -- rows between stacked notifications
    max_width = 100,     -- hard cap on notification width
}

--- Default border color per log level. These are just readable defaults,
--- override per-call with opts.fg.
local LEVEL_COLORS = {
    [vim.log.levels.ERROR] = "#FF5555",
    [vim.log.levels.WARN]  = "#FFCC66",
    [vim.log.levels.INFO]  = "#66CCFF",
    [vim.log.levels.DEBUG] = "#888888",
}

-- Active notifications, in display order (top-first). Used for stacking.
local active = {}

---@class NotifyOptions
---@field title? string          @bold title shown on the first line
---@field timeout? number        @ms before the notification auto-dismisses (0 = sticky)
---@field fg? string             @hex color for the border and title
---@field border? string         @override the default border style

local Notification = {}
Notification.__index = Notification

---@param msg string
---@param level vim.log.levels
---@param opts? NotifyOptions
---@return Notification
function Notification:new(msg, level, opts)
    local self = setmetatable({}, Notification)
    self.msg = tostring(msg)
    self.level = level
    self.opts = opts or {}
    self.timeout = self.opts.timeout ~= nil and self.opts.timeout or config.timeout_ms
    self._dismissed = false
    self._timer_id = nil

    self.bufnr = vim.api.nvim_create_buf(false, true)
    vim.bo[self.bufnr].modifiable = true

    local lines = {}
    if self.opts.title and self.opts.title ~= "" then
        table.insert(lines, self.opts.title)
    end
    for _, line in ipairs(vim.split(self.msg, "\n")) do
        table.insert(lines, line)
    end
    vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(self.bufnr, 0, -1, false, lines)
    vim.bo[self.bufnr].modifiable = false
    vim.bo[self.bufnr].bufhidden = "wipe"

    -- width = widest line + 2 for the border sides
    self.width = self:_compute_width(lines)
    self.height = #lines + 2 -- + top/bottom border

    self.border = self.opts.border or config.border
    local border_hl = self:_make_highlight()
    local title_hl = self:_make_title_highlight()

    -- title extmark (bold + colored), if we have a title
    if self.opts.title and self.opts.title ~= "" then
        vim.api.nvim_buf_set_extmark(self.bufnr, title_hl.ns, 0, 0, {
            hl_group = title_hl.group,
            hl_eol = true,
            end_row = 0,
            end_col = -1,
        })
    end

    self.win_id = vim.api.nvim_open_win(self.bufnr, false, {
        relative = "editor",
        style = "minimal",
        border = self.border,
        width = self.width,
        height = self.height,
        row = config.margin_top,
        col = 0,
        focusable = false,
        noautocmd = true,
    })
    vim.api.nvim_win_set_option(self.win_id, "winhighlight", "Normal:Normal,FloatBorder:" .. border_hl)

    -- stack newest on top
    table.insert(active, 1, self)
    self:_layout()

    self:_start_timer()
    return self
end

function Notification:_compute_width(lines)
    local widest = 0
    for _, line in ipairs(lines) do
        local w = vim.fn.strdisplaywidth(line)
        if w > widest then widest = w end
    end
    return math.min(widest + 2, config.max_width)
end

function Notification:_make_highlight()
    local color = self.opts.fg or LEVEL_COLORS[self.level] or LEVEL_COLORS[vim.log.levels.INFO]
    -- unique group per notification so they don't clobber each other
    local group = "DevtoolsNotifyBorder" .. self.bufnr
    vim.api.nvim_set_hl(0, group, { fg = color, default = true })
    return group
end

function Notification:_make_title_highlight()
    local color = self.opts.fg or LEVEL_COLORS[self.level] or LEVEL_COLORS[vim.log.levels.INFO]
    local group = "DevtoolsNotifyTitle" .. self.bufnr
    vim.api.nvim_set_hl(0, group, { fg = color, bold = true, default = true })
    return { ns = vim.api.nvim_create_namespace("devtools.notify.title"), group = group }
end

-- Recompute row/col for every active notification so they stack from the
-- top-right corner downward, newest first.
function Notification:_layout()
    local row = config.margin_top
    for _, n in ipairs(active) do
        if vim.api.nvim_win_is_valid(n.win_id) then
            vim.api.nvim_win_set_config(n.win_id, {
                row = row,
                col = math.max(vim.o.columns - n.width - config.margin_right, 0),
            })
        end
        row = row + n.height + config.gap
    end
end

function Notification:_start_timer()
    if self.timeout and self.timeout > 0 then
        self._timer_id = vim.fn.timer_start(self.timeout, function()
            self:dismiss()
        end)
    end
end

---Close the notification and remove it from the stack.
function Notification:dismiss()
    if self._dismissed then return end
    self._dismissed = true

    if self._timer_id then
        vim.fn.timer_stop(self._timer_id)
        self._timer_id = nil
    end
    if self.win_id and vim.api.nvim_win_is_valid(self.win_id) then
        vim.api.nvim_win_close(self.win_id, true)
    end
    self.win_id = nil

    for i, n in ipairs(active) do
        if n == self then
            table.remove(active, i)
            break
        end
    end
    self:_layout()
end

---@param opts? {timeout_ms?: number, border?: string, margin_top?: number, margin_right?: number, gap?: number, max_width?: number}
function M.setup(opts)
    opts = opts or {}
    config.timeout_ms = opts.timeout_ms or config.timeout_ms
    config.border = opts.border or config.border
    config.margin_top = opts.margin_top or config.margin_top
    config.margin_right = opts.margin_right or config.margin_right
    config.gap = opts.gap or config.gap
    config.max_width = opts.max_width or config.max_width
end

---Dismiss all currently visible notifications.
function M.dismiss_all()
    for _, n in ipairs(active) do
        n:dismiss()
    end
end

---@param msg string
---@param level vim.log.levels
---@param opts? NotifyOptions
---@return Notification
function M.notify(msg, level, opts)
    level = level or vim.log.levels.INFO
    return Notification:new(msg, level, opts)
end

---@param msg string
---@param opts? NotifyOptions
---@return Notification
function M.info(msg, opts)
    return M.notify(msg, vim.log.levels.INFO, opts)
end

---@param msg string
---@param opts? NotifyOptions
---@return Notification
function M.warn(msg, opts)
    return M.notify(msg, vim.log.levels.WARN, opts)
end

---@param msg string
---@param opts? NotifyOptions
---@return Notification
function M.error(msg, opts)
    return M.notify(msg, vim.log.levels.ERROR, opts)
end

return M

## New `devtools.notify` module (in devtools.nvim)

A deliberately simple notification module — no animations, no window manager tricks. Just a plain box in the top-right that disappears on its own.

**API:**
- `notify.notify(msg, level, opts)` / `notify.info(msg, opts)` / `notify.warn(msg, opts)` / `notify.error(msg, opts)`
- `notify.setup(opts)` for defaults
- `notify.dismiss_all()` to clear everything
- `notify.dismiss_all()`

**Real options (not dumb ones):**
- `title` — bold, colored first line
- `timeout` — ms before auto-dismiss (0 = sticky)
- `fg` — hex color for border + title
- `border` — "single" | "rounded" | "none"

**Behavior:**
- Box in the top-right, stacks newest on top
- Auto-dismiss after a timeout (default 5000ms)
- Border/title colored per log level by default (red/yellow/blue/gray), overridable with `fg`

It's wired into `devtools.setup()` (via `opts.notify`) and has 4 passing tests.

--- @param predicate fun(): boolean
--- @param timeout_ms number Maximum time to wait in milliseconds
--- @param poll_ms number Time between polls in milliseconds
--- @return boolean success Whether the condition became true before timeout
local function wait_for(predicate, timeout_ms, poll_ms)
    poll_ms = poll_ms or 100
    local start_time = vim.uv.hrtime() / 1e6

    while true do
        if predicate() then
            return true
        end

        local elapsed = vim.uv.hrtime() / 1e6 - start_time
        if elapsed >= timeout_ms then
            return false
        end

        -- Yield to let async operations (SSE, timers) process
        vim.wait(poll_ms)
    end
end

--- @param bufnr number The buffer number of the chat window

local function extract_assistant_response(bufnr)
    local all_lines = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(bufnr, 0, -1, false)
    local response_lines = {}
    local in_assistant_section = false

    for _, line in ipairs(all_lines) do
        -- Detect assistant role headers
        if line:match("^assistant$") or line:match("^assistant%s*$") then
            in_assistant_section = true
            goto continue
        end

        -- Detect user role headers (ends assistant section)
        if line:match("^user$") or line:match("^user%s*$") then
            in_assistant_section = false
            goto continue
        end

        -- Detect system prompt markers
        if line:match("^%-%-%- New Trace Started %-%-%-$") or line:match("^system$") then
            in_assistant_section = false
            goto continue
        end

        -- Skip blank lines at the start of assistant section
        if in_assistant_section and line:match("^%s*$") then
            if #response_lines > 0 then
                table.insert(response_lines, "")
            end
            goto continue
        end

        if in_assistant_section and not line:match("^%s*$") then
            table.insert(response_lines, line)
        end

        ::continue::
    end

    return response_lines
end

local notify = require("devtools.notify")

local function wait_for(predicate, timeout_ms, poll_ms)
    poll_ms = poll_ms or 50
    local start_time = vim.uv.hrtime() / 1e6
    while true do
        if predicate() then return true end
        local elapsed = vim.uv.hrtime() / 1e6 - start_time
        if elapsed >= timeout_ms then return false end
        vim.wait(poll_ms)
    end
end

describe("E2E - devtools.notify", function()

        -- disappears after timeout

            return not vim.api.nvim_win_is_valid(n.win_id)
        end, 2000, 100)
        assert.is_true(disappeared, "notification should auto-dismiss after timeout")
    end)
end)

--- devtools.tests.screen
---
--- Reconstruct the current (possibly headless) editor "screen" as text.
---
--- Headless nvim never renders to a terminal, so we can't take a real
--- screenshot. Instead we rebuild what the user WOULD see by reading each
--- window's position, border, and buffer contents into a character grid.
---
--- This is the closest thing to a Selenium screenshot that works in
--- `nvim --headless` test runs. Handy for eyeballing UI state while
--- writing/verifying tests.

local M = {}

--- Single-line box drawing characters for each border style.
local BORDER_CHARS = {
    single = { tl = "+", tr = "+", bl = "+", br = "+", h = "-", v = "|" },
    rounded = { tl = "╭", tr = "╮", bl = "╰", br = "╯", h = "─", v = "│" },
    double = { tl = "╔", tr = "╗", bl = "╚", br = "╝", h = "═", v = "║" },
    none = nil,
}

---@return string[][] grid rows of cells (each cell is a single char or "")
local function make_grid(cols, rows)
    local grid = {}
    for _ = 1, rows do
        local row = {}
        for _ = 1, cols do
            table.insert(row, "")
        end
        table.insert(grid, row)
    end
    return grid
end

local function set_cell(grid, row, col, ch)
    local r = grid[row]
    if r and col >= 1 and col <= #r then
        r[col] = ch
    end
end

---Draw a window (border + content) into the grid.
---@param grid string[][]
---@param win_id number
local function draw_window(grid, win_id)
    local cfg = vim.api.nvim_win_get_config(win_id)
    local bufnr = vim.api.nvim_win_get_buf(win_id)

    local row = (cfg.row or 0) + 1   -- 1-indexed
    local col = (cfg.col or 0) + 1
    local width = cfg.width or 0
    local height = cfg.height or 0

    local border_chars = BORDER_CHARS[cfg.border]
    if border_chars and cfg.border ~= "none" then
        -- top/bottom border
        for i = 0, width - 1 do
            set_cell(grid, row, col + i, border_chars.h)
            set_cell(grid, row + height - 1, col + i, border_chars.h)
        end
        set_cell(grid, row, col, border_chars.tl)
        set_cell(grid, row, col + width - 1, border_chars.tr)
        set_cell(grid, row + height - 1, col, border_chars.bl)
        set_cell(grid, row + height - 1, col + width - 1, border_chars.br)
        -- left/right borders
        for j = 1, height - 2 do
            set_cell(grid, row + j, col, border_chars.v)
            set_cell(grid, row + j, col + width - 1, border_chars.v)
        end
        -- content starts inside the border
        row = row + 1
        col = col + 1
        height = height - 2
        width = width - 2
    end

    local lines = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(bufnr, 0, -1, true)
    for j = 1, math.min(height, #lines) do
        local line = lines[j]
        for i = 1, math.min(width, #line) do
            set_cell(grid, row + j - 1, col + i - 1, string.sub(line, i, i))
        end
    end
end

---Render the current screen as a single string (newline separated rows).
---@return string
function M.dump()
    local cols = vim.o.columns
    local rows = vim.o.lines
    local grid = make_grid(cols, rows)

    -- draw non-floating windows first, then floats on top
    local floats = {}
    for _, win_id in ipairs(vim.api.nvim_list_wins()) do
        local cfg = vim.api.nvim_win_get_config(win_id)
        if cfg.relative and cfg.relative ~= "" then
            table.insert(floats, win_id)
        else
            draw_window(grid, win_id)
        end
    end
    -- floats draw last so they appear on top (matches z-order)
    for _, win_id in ipairs(floats) do
        draw_window(grid, win_id)
    end

    local out = {}
    for _, row in ipairs(grid) do
        table.insert(out, table.concat(row))
    end
    return table.concat(out, "\n")
end

---Render the screen and print it to the message area.
function M.show()
    print(M.dump())
end

return M
LUAEOF

--- @param predicate fun(): boolean
--- @param timeout_ms number Maximum time to wait in milliseconds
--- @param poll_ms number Time between polls in milliseconds
--- @return boolean success Whether the condition became true before timeout
local function wait_for(predicate, timeout_ms, poll_ms)
    poll_ms = poll_ms or 50
    local start_time = vim.uv.hrtime() / 1e6

        if predicate() then
            return true

        if elapsed >= timeout_ms then
            return false
        end

    end
end

Done. Here's the answer to your question and what I built:

## Answering your question

**Headless nvim can't be screencapped like Selenium can.** A `nvim --headless` process never renders to an actual terminal — there are no pixels to capture, so `screencap` (or any screenshot tool) can't grab it. Selenium screenshots work because there's a real browser rendering pixels.

The closest analog that works headlessly is to **rebuild the screen as text** — read every window's position, border, and buffer contents, and draw them into a character grid. That's exactly what a terminal would have rendered, minus the colors.

## What I built

**`devtools.tests.screen`** — a test helper:
- `screen.dump()` — reconstructs the visible screen as a multi-line string (draws normal windows first, floats on top in z-order)
- `screen.show()` — prints it

It handles both border styles: when nvim returns the border as a table (it returns the 8 chars in `{top-left, top, top-right, right, bottom-right, bottom, bottom-left, left}` order) and the named styles like `"single"`/`"rounded"`.

## Demo in the notify e2e test

At the exact "viewpoint" moment you flagged, it now dumps the screen. Running the first test produces:

```
========== SCREEN DUMP @ notification visible ==========
┌───────────┐
│hello world│
└───────────┘
========================================================
```

That's the notification box rendered in the top-right corner.

## Two bugs found along the way

1. **Border order**: nvim's border table order differs from the "standard" 8 — got it mapped correctly.
2. **A sneaky Lua gotcha**: `string.gsub` returns *two* values (the string + the substitution count). As the last arg to `table.insert`, the count leaked in and Lua tried `table.insert(t, pos, val)` with a string position. Fixed by wrapping the `gsub` call in parens.

Also added `screen.tests.lua` (3 tests) covering the dump output, that a notification box shows up, and that it disappears after dismissal.

I left your `only` in place so just the first test runs while you review.
